newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU Commission firm on Blair House oilseeds penalty.
newsitem.headline: EU Commission firm on Blair House oilseeds penalty.

text.p: The European Commission is not proposing any change to the way penalties for exceeding the Blair House oilseeds production area limit are applied, Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler has told EU farm ministers.
The ministers were divided at a meeting on Monday over demands for changes to the existing system, an EU official said.

"Both Portugal and Spain and the United Kingdom wanted penalties to apply equally to all member states rather than only to those responsible for exceeding the Blair House limit. Germany wanted no change," the official said.
The Blair House Agreement, signed in December 1992 between the EU and the United States, limits the production area for oilseeds to 4.934 million hectares based on a compulsory 10 per cent set-aside.

Currently, once the EU as a whole exceeds the limit by more than five percent, a penalty equal to a one percent reduction in area for every one percent above the limit is imposed on those member states responsible.
In its report to the Council and the European Parliament the Commission said that the current system prevented penalties disproportionate to production being imposed in certain member states.
"The European Commission does not for the moment, therefore, propose to amend the provisions concerned," the report said.
